title: 2B Reversal
teaches: The 2B bottom as we trade it: a stock breaks a prior swing low for the first time, goes no more than 3% under it and fails to follow through; the buy is a market order only after price trades back above the broken low, within 3 sessions, no more than 4% above it; the stop sits a few cents under the lowest low of the undercut, a close back under the broken low is a warning, a third comes off at 3R and 5R, and a market still making lower lows is not the place.

questions.q: Whose rule is the 2B?
choices: Victor Sperandeo
Larry Williams
Thomas Bulkowski
Linda Raschke
questions.answer: Victor Sperandeo
questions.why: Victor Sperandeo. Bulkowski credits him with the 2B pattern, and his rule says a failed break is apt to reverse the trend.
questions.lesson_line: The 2B is Sperandeo's rule: a break that fails.

wrong.Larry Williams: Williams gave us the Oops reversal, a one-day cousin of the 2B.
wrong.Thomas Bulkowski: Bulkowski measured the pattern but credits Sperandeo.
wrong.Linda Raschke: Connors and Raschke are known for Turtle Soup, a same-day cousin.

questions.q: A 2B bottom breaks a prior low, then fails and closes back above it.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The first break goes no more than 3% under the low and fails to follow through. The right valley sits below the left.
questions.lesson_line: A 2B is a break that fails. It dips under the low and reclaims it.

questions.q: When can you buy a 2B bottom?
choices: After it trades back above the low
As soon as it undercuts the low
On the second undercut of that low
At the next open after a new low
questions.answer: After it trades back above the low
questions.why: After it trades back above the broken low. Never before the reclaim. Buying the undercut itself is guessing.
questions.lesson_line: Wait for the reclaim. The undercut alone is not a trigger.

wrong.As soon as it undercuts the low: Buying the break before the reclaim is a named mistake.
wrong.On the second undercut of that low: The first break is the one that counts. A second undercut is not the trigger.
wrong.At the next open after a new low: A new low with no reclaim is a breakdown, not a 2B.

questions.q: You buy the 2B as soon as the low breaks, before any reclaim.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Never before the reclaim. Buying the undercut itself is guessing. We buy after it trades back above the low.
questions.lesson_line: No reclaim, no trade. Buying the undercut is guessing.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: Never buy a 2B more than ___% above the broken low.
questions.why: 4%. A buy more than 4% above the broken low is a chase. The stop would be too far away.
questions.lesson_line: Four percent over the low and I am done.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: Every 2B has a real stop order with the ___, and it only moves up.
questions.answer: broker
questions.why: Broker. Every position has a real stop order with the broker, not a stop kept in your head.
questions.lesson_line: A stop in your head is a debate. A stop with the broker is an appointment.

questions.q: A market still making lower lows with no reclaim is not the place for a 2B.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The best 2Bs come as the whole market undercuts its own lows and reclaims them. No reclaim, no 2B.
questions.lesson_line: Read the index first. A falling market is not a reclaim.

questions.q: How far may the undercut go under the broken low?
choices: 3% or less
7% or less
10% or less
Any depth if it reclaims
questions.answer: 3% or less
questions.why: 3% or less. A shallow undercut keeps the stop close. Deeper only with a smaller size or a later, tighter entry.
questions.lesson_line: Shallow undercut, close stop. Deep undercut, wide stop.

wrong.7% or less: That is more than twice the line. The stop is far wider than it looks.
wrong.10% or less: Far too deep. The stop would be a different trade.
wrong.Any depth if it reclaims: The reclaim does not fix a wide stop. Depth is a gate.

questions.q: A 2B reclaim day that closes in the lower half of its range still counts.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The reclaim day must close in the upper half of its range. A close in the bottom half invalidates it.
questions.lesson_line: A weak close on the reclaim day means the buyers did not hold.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: No close back above the broken low within ___ sessions: it is a breakdown, not a 2B.
questions.why: 3. No close back above the broken low within 3 sessions makes it a breakdown, not a 2B.
questions.lesson_line: Three sessions to reclaim. After that it is a breakdown.

questions.q: On a same-day reclaim, where does the stop go?
choices: A few cents under the day's low
At the old swing low of the setup
Under the 200-day average
At breakeven after the reclaim
questions.answer: A few cents under the day's low
questions.why: A few cents under the day's low. That is the lowest low of the undercut, the new extreme. Turtle Soup also puts its stop past the lower of the two days' lows.
questions.lesson_line: The stop goes just past the trap, under the new low.

wrong.At the old swing low of the setup: The old low sits above the new low. A stop there is inside the trap.
wrong.Under the 200-day average: The 200-day is context. The stop sits just past the new extreme.
wrong.At breakeven after the reclaim: Breakeven comes later, at the first trim.

questions.q: We take a 2B long even when the stock is under its 200-day.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. No longs below the 200-day, except a parabolic long. It is a hard rule.
questions.lesson_line: The 200-day line is a hard rule. No 2B longs under it.

questions.q: What is a 2B bottom, in one line?
choices: A first break of a low that fails fast
A gap down that reclaims the prior close
A 2 ATR flush on 2x volume
A break of the rising 50-day
questions.answer: A first break of a low that fails fast
questions.why: A first break of a prior low that fails fast. An Oops is judged on yesterday's low. A U&R is judged on a level like the 50-day.
questions.lesson_line: A 2B is a failed break of a swing low.

wrong.A gap down that reclaims the prior close: That is the Oops, judged on yesterday's low.
wrong.A 2 ATR flush on 2x volume: That is a capitulation, a different setup.
wrong.A break of the rising 50-day: A rising average as the level makes it a U&R.

questions.q: A 2B bottom gets you into a double bottom trade sooner, with more risk.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Bulkowski says it can get you in sooner than waiting for confirmation, but the risk of a failed trade is much greater.
questions.lesson_line: Sooner in means more failed trades. The stop is the exit.

questions.q: Where is a 2B at its best?
choices: At the 50-day or 200-day
In open air above the highs
Far under the 200-day
At a fresh high
questions.answer: At the 50-day or 200-day
questions.why: At the 50-day or 200-day. The best 2Bs undercut a low right at one of those big averages.
questions.lesson_line: A low at a big average is the best spot for the trap.

wrong.In open air above the highs: A 2B is a dip into a low, not a run in open air.
wrong.At a fresh high: A 2B bottom breaks a low, not a high.

questions.q: After you buy a 2B, a trade under the new low is the exit, at once.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A trade under the new low is the exit, and the stop only moves up. Take the loss at once.
questions.lesson_line: Under the new low, out at once. That is losing properly.

questions.q: How much comes off at the first trim, 3R?
choices: A third
Half
All of it
A quarter
questions.answer: A third
questions.why: A third. The hard rule is a third at 3R, another third at 5R, then trail the rest.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, a third at 5R, and trail the last third.

wrong.Half: The hard rule is a third, not half.
wrong.All of it: Trims are thirds. The last third is trailed.
wrong.A quarter: The hard rule is a third at 3R.

questions.q: Bought at 49.58 with the stop at 49.15. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 50.87. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add three of those to the fill. This is the RL trade, 3R on day 1.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open. The first third comes off there.

questions.q: What floor must a 2B stock clear?
choices: $10 a share and $20 million a day
$5 a share and $5 million a day
$2 a share and $10,000 a day traded
No floor for leaders
questions.answer: $10 a share and $20 million a day
questions.why: $10 a share and $20 million a day. Thin stocks are not even watched.
questions.lesson_line: Ten dollars a share, twenty million a day. Below that, no 2B.

wrong.$5 a share and $5 million a day: Too low. Our floor is $10 a share and $20 million a day.
wrong.$2 a share and $10,000 a day traded: Far under our floor of $10 and $20 million.

questions.q: A 2B is best when the stock's 200-day average is falling.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Best when the 200-day is higher than it was 20 sessions ago. SHOP sat near a rising 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: A rising 200-day under the low is a better floor.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The break is the ___ session to trade under that low since it formed.
questions.answer: first
questions.why: First. The break must be the first session to trade under that low since it formed. A later bounce is not it.
questions.lesson_line: Only the first break counts.

questions.q: Which lead-in to the low is clean?
choices: An orderly drift into the low
A big red news candle just before it
An outsized gap down the day before
questions.answer: An orderly drift into the low
questions.why: An orderly drift into the low. No outsized red news candle just before the break.
questions.lesson_line: A clean lead-in is a drift, not a news bar.

wrong.A big red news candle just before it: An outsized red news candle just before the break is not a clean lead-in.
wrong.An outsized gap down the day before: A news gap before the break is not an orderly drift.

questions.q: The prior swing low is 50.00 and the undercut low is 48.80. How deep is the undercut, in percent?
questions.why: 2.4%. The prior low minus the lowest low of the undercut, over the prior low. That fits the 3% line.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the undercut against the old low, and keep it inside 3%.

questions.q: Filled at 49.58 with the stop at 49.15. How far is the stop from the fill, in percent?
questions.why: 0.87%. Well inside the 3% line, so the stop is honest. This is the RL trade.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the stop. Inside about 3% is an honest stop.

questions.q: Where is the buy?
choices: 109.63, as it trades back above
108.30, the undercut low
110.50, a round number above
questions.story: A swing low sits at 109.62. Today the stock trades under it, then back above it in the same session.
questions.answer: 109.63, as it trades back above
questions.why: 109.63. A market order as it trades back above the low, a cent over it. That is how QCOM was bought on 2020-09-21.
questions.lesson_line: Buy as it trades back through the broken low, not before.

wrong.108.30, the undercut low: That is buying the undercut itself, before the reclaim.
wrong.110.50, a round number above: A round number above is a chase. Buy as it trades back through the low.

questions.q: Where does the stop go?
choices: 108.25, just under today's low
109.62, at the old swing low
109.00, halfway to the old low
Under the 200-day average
questions.story: You buy the reclaim of the 109.62 low at 109.63. Today's low, the undercut, was 108.30.
questions.answer: 108.25, just under today's low
questions.why: 108.25. A few cents under today's low of 108.30, the lowest low of the undercut. That was QCOM's 1.26% stop.
questions.lesson_line: The stop sits just under the new low, the point the trap was set.

wrong.109.62, at the old swing low: The old low is above the undercut low. A stop there sits inside the trap.
wrong.109.00, halfway to the old low: A halfway stop is a guess. The stop sits past the new extreme.
wrong.Under the 200-day average: The 200-day is context, not the stop.

questions.q: Can you buy the open?
choices: Yes, it is inside 4% above the low
No, never buy a gap
No, wait for a pullback to the low
Yes, but only half size
questions.story: The break day undercut the 64.00 low and closed back above it. The next morning it opens at 65.30.
questions.answer: Yes, it is inside 4% above the low
questions.why: Yes. The open is inside the 4% limit above the broken low, so a market order at the open is fine.
questions.lesson_line: Inside 4% over the low, the open is a fair fill.

wrong.No, never buy a gap: A gap inside the 4% limit is fine.
wrong.No, wait for a pullback to the low: Waiting can miss it; the open is inside the limit.
wrong.Yes, but only half size: Size comes from the stop, not from the gap.

questions.q: Can you buy the open?
choices: No, it is over 4% above the low
Yes, a gap up shows real strength
Yes, with a smaller stop to fit
Yes, at half size
questions.story: The broken low is 40.00. The stock closed back above it yesterday. Now it gaps open at 42.00.
questions.answer: No, it is over 4% above the low
questions.why: No. 42.00 is more than 4% above the broken low. Never chase; the stop stays under the new low and the shares shrink.
questions.lesson_line: Past 4% over the low, the open is not ours.

wrong.Yes, a gap up shows real strength: Strength is not a reason to chase.
wrong.Yes, with a smaller stop to fit: You do not tighten the stop to fit.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size does not change the rule.

questions.q: Which of these is a breakdown or a Remount, not a 2B?
choices: Six closes under, then recovery
It reclaims later the same day
It reclaims on the next day
It undercuts by 1% and reclaims
questions.answer: Six closes under, then recovery
questions.why: Six closes under the low. A 2B closes back above within 3 sessions; five or more closes under it is a Remount.
questions.lesson_line: Quick reclaim is a 2B. A long stay under the line is not.

wrong.It reclaims later the same day: A same-day reclaim is the quickest version of the 2B.
wrong.It reclaims on the next day: A reclaim in a day or two is inside the window.
wrong.It undercuts by 1% and reclaims: A shallow undercut is what we want.

questions.q: Do you buy it?
choices: No, a report is inside 3 sessions
Yes, it is a 2B, not earnings
Yes, at half size
Yes, then sell before the report
questions.story: A clean 2B reclaims its low. The company reports earnings in two sessions.
questions.answer: No, a report is inside 3 sessions
questions.why: No. No new buys in the 3 days before a report. A report this close can gap the stock past your stop.
questions.lesson_line: No new buys in the 3 days before a report.

wrong.Yes, it is a 2B, not earnings: The report window is its own rule.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size does not change the rule.
wrong.Yes, then sell before the report: The rule is no new buys inside the window.

questions.q: Do you take it?
choices: Pass; the market is still falling
Take it at full size on the reclaim
Take it, the leader is strong
Take it with a tighter stop
questions.story: A leader undercuts a low by 0.75% and reclaims it the same day. The Nasdaq made another lower low today, with no reclaim.
questions.answer: Pass; the market is still falling
questions.why: Pass for now. A market still making lower lows is not the place. Buying a 2B then is a named mistake, as NVDA and AMD showed in April 2024.
questions.lesson_line: A clean 2B in a falling market is still a falling market.

wrong.Take it at full size on the reclaim: A market still making lower lows is not the place.
wrong.Take it, the leader is strong: Strength in one name did not save NVDA or AMD.
wrong.Take it with a tighter stop: You never tighten the stop to fit.

questions.q: Your plan from here?
choices: Hold to the stop; do not add
Sell at the close to be safe
Add on the dip to lower the cost
Move the stop under 99.40
questions.story: You bought the reclaim at 100.05, with the stop at 98.70. The next day it closes at 99.40, back under the 100.00 low, above your stop.
questions.answer: Hold to the stop; do not add
questions.why: Hold to the stop and do not add. A close back under the broken low is a warning that the failure has failed. Look at TSLA, 2023-08-11.
questions.lesson_line: A close back under the low is a warning. The stop does the rest.

wrong.Sell at the close to be safe: The stop is the exit, not a scary close.
wrong.Add on the dip to lower the cost: We never add after a warning.

questions.q: Your plan from here?
choices: Take the loss; retry on a trigger
Wish you had used a wider stop
Buy back at once with the same stop
Move the stop lower next time
questions.story: You bought at 30.83 with the stop at 30.26. The next day's low touches the stop to the cent and you are out. Twenty sessions later the stock is higher.
questions.answer: Take the loss; retry on a trigger
questions.why: Take the loss. The stop did its job. A new try needs a new trigger. MGM, bought 2017-07-05, touched the stop to the cent the next day.
questions.lesson_line: A stop-out is the plan working. Re-enter only on a new trigger.

wrong.Wish you had used a wider stop: A wider stop is a bigger loss. The stop did its job.
wrong.Buy back at once with the same stop: Buy again only on a new trigger.
wrong.Move the stop lower next time: A stop never moves down or wider.

questions.q: What do you do now?
choices: Out at once; the loss is past 2R
Hold, the new stop is 96.40
Keep the stop at 98.70 and wait
Buy more at 96.40 to average down
questions.story: You bought at 100.05 with the stop at 98.70. It gaps open at 97.00. The first 30-minute low is 96.40. Your risk was 1.35 a share.
questions.answer: Out at once; the loss is past 2R
questions.why: Out at once. At the first 30-minute low the loss is well past 2R. Inside 2R that low is the new stop; past it, you leave.
questions.lesson_line: On a gap through the stop, the first 30 minutes decide.

wrong.Hold, the new stop is 96.40: That would be right inside 2R. This low is past 2R.
wrong.Buy more at 96.40 to average down: We never add to a loser.

questions.q: Fill 50.01 and stop 48.75. How far is the stop from the fill, in percent?
questions.why: 2.5%. Inside the usual 3% line, so the stop fits at full size.
questions.lesson_line: Check the stop against 3% before you size.

questions.q: Bought at 42.89 with the stop at 42.37. Where is 5R?
questions.why: 45.49. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add five of those to the fill. This is the DINO trade.
questions.lesson_line: Know 3R and 5R before the open.

questions.q: At 3R, what comes off?
choices: Sell a third, stop to breakeven
Sell it all and take the win
Sell half, keep the original stop
Hold all, nudge the stop up
questions.story: You bought at 49.58 with the stop at 49.15. The 2B reaches 3R.
questions.answer: Sell a third, stop to breakeven
questions.why: Sell a third and move the stop to breakeven. The first trim is a third at 3R.
questions.lesson_line: At 3R sell a third and lift the stop to breakeven.

wrong.Sell it all and take the win: Trims are thirds, and the last third is trailed.
wrong.Sell half, keep the original stop: The hard rule is a third.
wrong.Hold all, nudge the stop up: The first third comes off at 3R.

questions.q: Your call on day 10?
choices: Sell it and free the money
Hold on, aiming for 5R
Add if it breaks out higher
Widen the stop to give it room
questions.story: It is day 10. The 2B has chopped sideways at +0.7R. The stop has not been touched.
questions.answer: Sell it and free the money
questions.why: Sell it. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money.
questions.lesson_line: Ten days and under 1R: sell and use the money elsewhere.

wrong.Hold on, aiming for 5R: A trade under 1R after 10 days is sold.

questions.q: How many do you buy?
choices: A few, then add as they work
All four at full size
One, at double the normal size
None until next month
questions.story: After a correction the market reading turns Green again. Four 2Bs reclaim their lows in one morning.
questions.answer: A few, then add as they work
questions.why: A few. After a correction, when the reading turns Green again, start with a few. Add more only as the first ones work.
questions.lesson_line: Back from a correction, start small and add as they work.

wrong.All four at full size: Start with a few and add only as they work.
wrong.One, at double the normal size: Fewer names never means a bigger size. Size comes from each stop.
wrong.None until next month: Green again is when 2Bs work best, with a few positions.

questions.q: When do you take the first trim?
choices: At the open, 51.40
At the close
When it falls back to 50.87
Wait for 5R
questions.story: Your 3R level is 50.87. The next morning the 2B opens at 51.40.
questions.answer: At the open, 51.40
questions.why: At the open, 51.40. If a day opens above a trim level, take that trim at the open.
questions.lesson_line: Open past the level, take the trim at the open.

wrong.At the close: The rule is to take it at the open.
wrong.When it falls back to 50.87: You may never get that price back.
wrong.Wait for 5R: The first third comes off at 3R. The open is past it.

questions.q: Which average is the default trail for a steadier name?
choices: The 21-day
The 50-day
The 200-day
The 5-day
questions.answer: The 21-day
questions.why: The 21-day. Sell on a close below it. Fast movers trail the 10-day.
questions.lesson_line: Steadier name, 21-day. Fast mover, 10-day. Sell on a close below.

wrong.The 50-day: Too slow for the default trail.
wrong.The 200-day: That is the long-term line, far too slow for a trail.
wrong.The 5-day: The defaults are the 10-day and the 21-day.

questions.q: How do you play it?
choices: Take it only if it is an A+
Take it at full size, as in Green
Pass, only Green allows it
Short the market instead
questions.story: A clean 2B reclaims its low, but the market reading is Orange.
questions.answer: Take it only if it is an A+
questions.why: Take it only as an A+. In an Orange market only A+ setups. Green is full risk, Yellow smaller and fewer.
questions.lesson_line: Orange market, A+ only. Yellow, smaller. Green, full.

wrong.Pass, only Green allows it: Orange allows an A+, so Green is not the only reading that does.
wrong.Short the market instead: Red is mostly cash and shorts. Orange still allows an A+ long.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Mostly cash; no 2B longs
Take it at full size
Take it at half size
Take it with a tighter stop
questions.story: A clean 2B reclaims its low, but the market reading is Red.
questions.answer: Mostly cash; no 2B longs
questions.why: Mostly cash. In a Red market it is mostly cash, plus shorts below the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: Red market: cash first. The 2B waits.

wrong.Take it at half size: In Red the answer is mostly cash.
wrong.Take it with a tighter stop: A tighter stop does not fix the market.

questions.q: Sperandeo says an intermediate 2B usually fails within three to five weeks.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Bulkowski quotes Sperandeo: for intermediate highs or lows, the new extreme will usually break within three to five days.
questions.lesson_line: The originator says three to five days. Ours is a reclaim within 3 sessions.

questions.q: You may hold a 2B through a report only if the trade is up 5R.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. No new buys in the 3 days before a report. Hold through one only if the trade is up 5R.
questions.lesson_line: Through a report only with a 5R cushion.

questions.q: 2B or Oops?
choices: An Oops, judged on yesterday's low
A 2B, it reclaimed the same day
A U&R, it undercut a level
questions.story: Yesterday closed at 80.00 with a low of 79.20. Today opens at 79.60, trades down to 78.90 and closes at 80.40.
questions.answer: An Oops, judged on yesterday's low
questions.why: An Oops. It opened under the prior close, broke yesterday's low and reclaimed the prior close the same day. The reference is one day old.
questions.lesson_line: Count the age of the broken low. One day old is an Oops.

wrong.A 2B, it reclaimed the same day: A 2B breaks a swing low at least 5 sessions old. This broke yesterday's low.
wrong.A U&R, it undercut a level: A U&R needs a bigger level than yesterday's low.

questions.q: 2B or Oops?
choices: A 2B, the broken low is old
An Oops, it reclaimed a close
A Remount, it took two days
questions.story: On Tuesday the stock breaks a swing low that is eight sessions old. It closes back above that low on Wednesday.
questions.answer: A 2B, the broken low is old
questions.why: A 2B. The broken low is eight sessions old, and the reclaim came in 2 sessions. An Oops breaks yesterday's low.
questions.lesson_line: An older swing low and a reclaim in a day or two: that is a 2B.

wrong.An Oops, it reclaimed a close: An Oops breaks yesterday's low and reclaims the prior close the same day.
wrong.A Remount, it took two days: A Remount follows five or more closes under the level.

questions.q: 2B or Oops?
choices: A 2B, the reference low is old
An Oops, it reclaimed the same day
A Remount, the low is old
questions.story: The stock opens above yesterday's close, then dips under a nine-session-old swing low and closes back above it the same day.
questions.answer: A 2B, the reference low is old
questions.why: A 2B. An Oops opens under the prior close and is judged on yesterday's low. This one opened above it and broke an older swing low.
questions.lesson_line: The open and the reference low decide it. Old swing low, 2B.

wrong.An Oops, it reclaimed the same day: An Oops opens under the prior close. This one opened above it.
wrong.A Remount, the low is old: A Remount needs five or more closes under the level.

questions.q: 2B or U&R?
choices: A U&R, the level is an average
A 2B, it reclaimed the line
An Oops, it dipped and recovered
questions.story: A leader dips under its rising 50-day average and closes back above it. There was no swing low nearby.
questions.answer: A U&R, the level is an average
questions.why: A U&R. When the level is a rising average, a prior high, a round number or the range low, it is a U&R. A 2B breaks a swing low.
questions.lesson_line: Name the level. A swing low is a 2B. A rising average is a U&R.

wrong.A 2B, it reclaimed the line: A 2B breaks a prior swing low, not an average.
wrong.An Oops, it dipped and recovered: An Oops needs a break of yesterday's low.

questions.q: 2B or Remount?
choices: A Remount, bought on the retake
A 2B, it reclaimed the low
An Oops, it recovered fast
questions.story: The stock closed under an old low for six sessions. Today it retakes the line.
questions.answer: A Remount, bought on the retake
questions.why: A Remount. Six closes under the 236.64 low before the first close back above. That was GS on 2017-01-25.
questions.lesson_line: Count the closes under the line. Five or more is a Remount.

wrong.A 2B, it reclaimed the low: A 2B closes back above within 3 sessions. Six closes under is too long.
wrong.An Oops, it recovered fast: An Oops is judged on yesterday's low.

questions.q: 2B or a spring?
choices: A spring, the level is a floor
A 2B, it reclaimed a swing low
An Oops, it closed back inside
questions.story: A stock has traded sideways for 20 sessions and touched its floor three times. It dips under the floor and closes back inside the same day.
questions.answer: A spring, the level is a floor
questions.why: A spring. The level is the floor of a sideways range of 15 sessions or more, touched at least twice. A 2B breaks a single swing low.
questions.lesson_line: A range floor is a spring. A single swing low is a 2B.

wrong.A 2B, it reclaimed a swing low: A 2B's level is a single swing low, not the floor of a range.
wrong.An Oops, it closed back inside: An Oops is judged on yesterday's low.

questions.q: Is it a 2B?
choices: No, there is no prior swing low
Yes, it dipped and reclaimed
Yes, it is a Remount
questions.story: A stock falls for six days in a row. Today it dips under yesterday's low and closes a little higher.
questions.answer: No, there is no prior swing low
questions.why: No. A one-day dip under yesterday's low in a straight decline is not a 2B. The level must be at least 5 sessions old.
questions.lesson_line: Calling any dip under yesterday's low a 2B is a mistake.

wrong.Yes, it dipped and reclaimed: A dip under yesterday's low is not a 2B.
wrong.Yes, it is a Remount: A Remount follows five or more closes under a level.

questions.q: Is it a 2B?
choices: No, it is not the first break
Yes, it reclaimed the low
Yes, a second try is stronger
questions.story: Last week the stock traded under a swing low and bounced. This week it dips under the same low again and closes back above it.
questions.answer: No, it is not the first break
questions.why: No. The break must be the first session under the low since it formed. A bounce in a decline that reclaims again is not a 2B.
questions.lesson_line: Only the first break of the low counts.

wrong.Yes, it reclaimed the low: The reclaim is not enough. The break must be the first.

questions.q: Which rule fails?
choices: The undercut was deeper than 3%
The low was too old
It did not close back above
It was the first break
questions.story: A stock closes back above its swing low within 3 sessions. The lowest low of the undercut went 4.36% under the old low.
questions.answer: The undercut was deeper than 3%
questions.why: The undercut. It went 4.36% under the low, past 3%, and the stop is 4.83% away. That was DELL on 2024-07-22.
questions.lesson_line: A deep undercut is not a 2B at full size.

wrong.The low was too old: Age is not the failing number.
wrong.It did not close back above: It did close back above the low.
wrong.It was the first break: Being the first break is good.

questions.q: Why is the reclaim not a trigger?
choices: The reclaim closed in the bottom half
The gap was too big
The low was too old
The break was too shallow
questions.story: A gap opens over the broken low, then sells off all day. The close sits at 0.14 of the day's range.
questions.answer: The reclaim closed in the bottom half
questions.why: The reclaim day closed at 0.14 of its range. A close in the bottom half invalidates it. That was GOOG on 2026-07-20.
questions.lesson_line: A reclaim that sells off all day is not a reclaim.

wrong.The gap was too big: The gap is not the failing number.
wrong.The low was too old: Age is not the failing number.
wrong.The break was too shallow: A shallow break is what we want.

questions.q: Why do the rules skip it?
choices: The close is under the 200-day
The undercut was too deep
The reclaim took too many sessions
The low was too young
questions.story: A same-day undercut and reclaim of a 638.61 low. The close is 4.2% under the 200-day average.
questions.answer: The close is under the 200-day
questions.why: The close is under the 200-day. META on 2026-01-08 closed 4.2% below it. No longs below the 200-day. That one paid, so the rule is about odds.
questions.lesson_line: A 2B shape under the 200-day is watch only.

questions.q: What did the daily chart miss?
choices: The market had not stopped falling
The undercut was too deep
The 200-day was falling
The reclaim took too long
questions.story: A leader undercuts a low by 0.75% and closes under it. The next morning it opens over the low and you buy at 77.98. The next day it falls through your stop.
questions.answer: The market had not stopped falling
questions.why: The market had not stopped falling. PYPL reclaimed on 2018-03-26 and fell through its stop the next day. SPY made a lower low days later.
questions.lesson_line: The chart looks clean. The index is the tell.

wrong.The 200-day was falling: The index, not the 200-day, was the problem.

questions.q: What told you the trade had failed?
choices: The open traded under the new low
The reclaim day closed near the high
The undercut was shallow
The volume was light on the reclaim
questions.story: You bought the same-day reclaim of the 240.70 low at 240.71. Your stop is 237.97, a few cents under the undercut low. The next session opens at 235.70.
questions.answer: The open traded under the new low
questions.why: The open traded under the new low. After the 2023-08-11 reclaim, TSLA opened at 235.70, under the stop. The failure failed.
questions.lesson_line: A trade under the new low is the exit, at once.

wrong.The reclaim day closed near the high: A strong close was not the failure.

questions.q: What went wrong, and what is the fix?
choices: Stop over 3% in a falling market
The undercut was too deep
The reclaim day closed low
The low was too young
questions.story: NVDA reclaimed the same day at 83.03 with the stop at 82.35. The next day it fell to 75.61 as the index made a lower low.
questions.answer: Stop over 3% in a falling market
questions.why: Cut, kept for the record. The stop was only 0.82% away, so it was never a wide-stop trade. NVDA fell 10% the day after its 2024-04-18 reclaim in a falling market.
questions.lesson_line: Cut: the stop-width premise did not survive the rescan.

questions.q: Full size?
choices: No; the stop is much too wide
Yes, the reclaim is strong enough
Yes, with the stop at the old low
Buy the undercut instead
questions.story: A leader undercuts its 74.57 low to 66.12 and closes back above the low the next day.
questions.answer: No; the stop is much too wide
questions.why: No. A deep undercut at full size is a named mistake. PLTR undercut its 74.57 low by 11.3%, so a stop beyond the new low sits far away.
questions.lesson_line: The deeper the undercut, the wider the stop.

wrong.Yes, the reclaim is strong enough: A strong reclaim does not make the stop closer.
wrong.Yes, with the stop at the old low: The stop goes past the new low, not at the old one.

questions.q: Why take a third at 3R on this one?
choices: It banks gain before the stall
It guarantees the whole move
It lowers the stop
It lets you add to the position
questions.story: A 2B reaches 3R on day 2, then stalls for weeks before it runs.
questions.answer: It banks gain before the stall
questions.why: It banks gain before the stall. JBL reached 3R on day 2, then sat near +4% after 20 sessions. That is the case for the trims.
questions.lesson_line: Slow to pay is still a win if you took the third at 3R.

wrong.It guarantees the whole move: No trim guarantees anything. It banks a third.
wrong.It lowers the stop: The stop only moves up, to breakeven at the first trim.
wrong.It lets you add to the position: We buy once. A trim never makes room to add.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, today. It undercut a swing low and closed back above it. Take it or pass?
choices: Take it; same-day reclaim, strong close
Pass; the undercut was too deep
Pass; the close is in the bottom half
questions.answer: Take it; same-day reclaim, strong close
questions.why: Take it. The stock undercut a nine-session-old low and reclaimed it the same session, closing in the top 6% of its range. 3R came the next day.
questions.lesson_line: A strong close on the reclaim day is the sign to look for.

wrong.Pass; the close is in the bottom half: The close was in the top 6% of the range.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, today. It gapped over a broken low. Take it or pass?
choices: Pass; the reclaim closed near its low
Take it; the gap shows strength
Take it; the low is old
questions.answer: Pass; the reclaim closed near its low
questions.why: Pass. The gap over the level sold off all day and closed at 0.14 of its range. A close in the bottom half invalidates it.
questions.lesson_line: A reclaim that closes near the low is a failed reclaim.

wrong.Take it; the gap shows strength: The gap faded all day. Strength has to hold to the close.
wrong.Take it; the low is old: The age of the low is fine. The close is the failing number.

questions.q: The 2B shape alone is enough to make money.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Expecting the shape alone to pay is a named mistake. The market, the stop and the entry all matter.
questions.lesson_line: A shape is one filter. The market and the stop are the others.

questions.q: What do you do with the last third?
choices: Sell it; it closed under the trail
Hold, it is still above the 50-day
Add back the thirds you sold
Move the stop down to give room
questions.story: You sold a third at 3R and a third at 5R. The steadier stock now closes under its 21-day average.
questions.answer: Sell it; it closed under the trail
questions.why: Sell it. The last third trails the 21-day for a steadier name, and a close below it is the exit.
questions.lesson_line: Trail the last third and sell on a close below the average.

wrong.Hold, it is still above the 50-day: The 50-day is not the trail for a steadier name. The 21-day is.
wrong.Add back the thirds you sold: We buy once and never add back.
wrong.Move the stop down to give room: A stop never moves down or wider.
